learningObjective: The map gives direct node access while the doubly linked order exposes the eviction candidate at its left edge.

mechanismReview.pattern: Hash map for direct lookup plus a sentinel-based doubly linked list for recency order.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: The interface requires both O(1) key lookup and O(1) least-recent eviction, which no single ordinary array, map, or queue provides alone.
mechanismReview.invariant: Every map entry points to exactly one node between the sentinels, and list order is least-recent to most-recent; successful access moves that same key to the right edge.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Retain capacity, the key-to-node map, least/most sentinels, and each node’s previous/next links. Remove and append are constant-size pointer rewires.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: A sentinel-bounded linked chain gives every cache node a stable motion key as it moves, while adjacent visible map state shows direct key-to-node lookup through every mutation.
rejectedAlternatives: A map alone cannot identify the least-recent key in O(1) time.
A queue alone cannot find and move an arbitrary accessed key in O(1) time.
A final-state-only diagram hides the temporary over-capacity state and the separate list removal and map deletion.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: Combine an index with an ordered linked structure whenever a system needs direct identity lookup plus constant-time promotion, removal, or boundary eviction.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.
